parsed.title: Optimal covering ratio conjecture for the infinite square grid
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be an infinite square grid, and let $D$ be a pebble distribution on $G$. Say that a vertex is reachable from $D$ if pebbles can be moved to it under the pebbling rules, and let the **covering ratio** of $D$ be the ratio of the distribution's size to the number of vertices it covers. **Optimal covering ratio conjecture.** If every vertex of $G$ is reachable from $D$, then the covering ratio of $D$ is at most $3.5$. The paper gives periodic distributions whose covering ratios converge to $3.5$, so this bound would be best possible; the earlier bound $3.25$ was thereby disproved.
parsed.source_name: Ervin Győri, Gyula Y. Katona and László F. Papp, “Constructions for the optimal pebbling of grids”, arXiv:1601.02229 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.02229

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

parsed.title: The strong rationality characterization for permutation classes
parsed.statement:
A **permutation class** is a class of permutations closed under taking patterns. A class is **strongly rational** if it and all of its subclasses have rational generating functions, and it is **well-quasi-ordered** if its permutations are well-quasi-ordered under pattern containment.

**Strong rationality conjecture.** A permutation class is strongly rational if and only if it is well-quasi-ordered and does not contain the class of $312$-avoiding permutations or any symmetry of it.

This conjecture seeks to characterize strong rationality using structural properties of permutation classes. The stated results establish the analogous characterization for subclasses of the $321$-avoiding permutations, while the general assertion remains open.
parsed.source_name: Michael H. Albert, Robert Brignall, Nik Ruškuc and Vincent Vatter, “Rationality for subclasses of 321-avoiding permutations”, arXiv:1602.00672 (2019).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.00672

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2016).

parsed.title: Upper growth rates are realized by sum closed classes
parsed.statement:
Let an **upper growth rate** of a permutation class mean a real number that occurs as the upper exponential growth rate of that class, and let a **sum closed class** be a permutation class closed under direct sum. **Upper growth-rate conjecture.** Every upper growth rate of a permutation class is the growth rate of a sum closed class.

The conjecture would reduce the characterization of upper growth rates to sum closed classes, extending the paper's growth-rate methods. The source places it among the remaining steps toward a complete characterization of growth rates; the stated gap in the surrounding results is approximately $0.05176$.
parsed.source_name: Vincent Vatter, “Growth rates of permutation classes: from countable to uncountable”, arXiv:1605.04297 (2019).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.04297

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

parsed.title: The four-antipalindrome conjecture
parsed.statement:
An **antipalindrome** is a natural number whose canonical base-$2$ expansion equals the complement of its reversal. The claim concerns all even natural numbers.

**Four-antipalindrome conjecture.** Every even natural number is the sum of at most $4$ antipalindromes.

The source says that the conditional bound of $13$ is probably far from optimal and that numerical evidence supports this stronger bound. No proof is given, so the conjecture remains open.
parsed.source_name: Aayush Rajasekaran, Jeffrey Shallit and Tim Smith, “Sums of Palindromes: an Approach via Automata”, arXiv:1706.10206 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.10206

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

parsed.title: The exceptional three-antipalindrome conjecture
parsed.statement:
An **antipalindrome** is a natural number whose canonical base-$2$ expansion equals the complement of its reversal. Let

$$
E=\{8,18,28,130,134,138,148,158,176,318,530,538,548,576,644,1300,2170,2202,2212,2228,2230,2248,8706,8938,8948,34970,35082\}.
$$

**Exceptional three-antipalindrome conjecture.** Every even natural number outside $E$ is the sum of at most $3$ antipalindromes.

The claim is presented as a numerical conjecture refining the preceding four-antipalindrome bound. The listed exceptions are the only exceptions asserted by the source, and no proof or resolution is provided.
parsed.source_name: Aayush Rajasekaran, Jeffrey Shallit and Tim Smith, “Sums of Palindromes: an Approach via Automata”, arXiv:1706.10206 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.10206

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

parsed.title: Doyle–Faber–Krumm conjecture on quadratic-field preperiodic graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $K$ be a quadratic number field, let $f_c(x)=x^2+c$ with $c\in K$, and let $G(f_c,K)$ be the directed graph of $K$-rational preperiodic points, with an edge $\alpha\to f_c(\alpha)$. **Doyle–Faber–Krumm quadratic-field graph conjecture.** The graph $G(f_c,K)$ is isomorphic to one of the $46$ directed graphs appearing in the cited appendix; in particular, 
$$
|\operatorname{PrePer}(f_c,K)|\leq 15.
$$
 This is computationally supported and concerns the degree-two case of the quadratic-polynomial uniform boundedness conjecture. The source presents it as evidence-based and does not state a proof.
parsed.source_name: John R. Doyle, “Dynamical modular curves for quadratic polynomial maps”, arXiv:1707.02257 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.02257

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2017).

parsed.title: Amini's mak–stat equidistribution conjecture for pattern-avoiding permutations
parsed.statement: For a pattern $\tau$, let $S_n(\tau)$ denote the set of permutations in $S_n$ avoiding $\tau$. The statistics $mak$ and $stat$ are generalized-pattern statistics, and equidistribution means equality of their generating polynomials on the indicated avoidance classes. **Amini's mak–stat conjecture.** The statistic $mak$ over $S_n(132)$, $S_n(213)$, $S_n(231)$, and $S_n(312)$ is equidistributed, respectively, with $stat$ over $S_n(213)$, $S_n(231)$, $S_n(231)$, and $S_n(213)$. This is one of Amini's conjectures concerning Mahonian statistics on pattern-avoiding permutations; the supplied text does not give a resolution.
parsed.source_name: Joanna N. Chen, “Equidistributions of MAJ and STAT over pattern avoiding permutations”, arXiv:1707.07195 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.07195

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2017).

parsed.title: FindStat's double-deficiency refinement for Dyck paths
parsed.statement:
Let $D$ be a Dyck path, let $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal N$ be the statistics defined from its row-area and column-area sequences, and let $\pi$ be the $321$-avoiding permutation associated with $D$ by the Billey-Jockusch-Stanley bijection. A **double deficiency** is the permutation statistic referenced in the source.

**Double-deficiency refinement.** For a Dyck path $D$, an index $k$ is in $\mathcal F$ but not in $\mathcal N\cap\mathcal D$ if and only if it is a double deficiency in the $321$-avoiding permutation $\pi$ associated with $D$ using the Billey-Jockusch-Stanley bijection.

The source describes this as a common refinement of both parts of Marczinzik's conjecture and proves it using the Billey-Jockusch-Stanley bijection, so it is solved in the paper.
parsed.source_name: Martin Rubey and Christian Stump, “Double deficiencies of Dyck paths via the Billey-Jockusch-Stanley bijection”, arXiv:1708.05092 (2017).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.05092

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of August 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

parsed.title: The equal-parameter Armstrong conjecture for simultaneous bicores
parsed.statement:
Let $s$ be a positive integer and let $a,b$ satisfy $0\leq a,b<s$. For parameters $r$ and $c$, write $\mathcal{C}_{(r\,|\,0,c)}$ for the corresponding set of bipartitions, and let the size of a bipartition mean the total number of boxes in its two components. **Equal-parameter Armstrong conjecture.** If $s$ and $a-b$ are coprime, then the average size of a bipartition in

$$
\mathcal{C}_{(s\,|\,0,a)}\cap\mathcal{C}_{(s\,|\,0,b)}
$$

is

$$
\frac{(s+1)(a(s-a)+b(s-b)+1-s)}{12}.
$$

This is proposed as an analogue of Armstrong's conjecture for simultaneous core bipartitions; the case $a=0$ recovers Armstrong's conjecture for ordinary simultaneous cores. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
parsed.source_name: Matthew Fayers, “Simultaneous core multipartitions”, arXiv:1709.00079 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.00079

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2017).

parsed.title: A bipartite-subgraph-free bound for pebbling numbers of direct graph products
parsed.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be connected graphs, with $G\ne K_1$ and $H$ nonbipartite. Let $G\times H$ denote the direct product of graphs, and let $\pi(G)$ denote the pebbling number.

**Direct-product pebbling conjecture.**

$$
\pi(G\times H)\leq \frac{9}{16}\pi(G)\pi(H)^2.
$$

The conjecture seeks to remove the use of chosen connected spanning bipartite subgraphs from the preceding results for direct products. The paper presents the inequality as an expected analogous bound, and it remains unresolved in the source.
parsed.source_name: John Asplund, Glenn Hurlbert and Franklin Kenter, “Pebbling on Graph Products and other Binary Graph Constructions”, arXiv:1801.07808 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.07808

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

parsed.title: Bean–Tannock–Ulfarsson purity conjecture for boundary-grid downcore graphs
parsed.statement: Let $\pi$ be a $123$-avoiding permutation, and let its boundary grid be the associated skew Young diagram. The **downcore graph** has the boxes of the boundary grid as vertices, with an edge between $(i,j)$ and $(k,\ell)$ when either $i<k$ and $j>\ell$, or $i>k$ and $j<\ell$, and both opposite-corner boxes $(i,\ell)$ and $(k,j)$ lie in the skew Young diagram. A graph is **pure** if every maximal independent set has the same size. **Bean–Tannock–Ulfarsson's purity conjecture.** The downcore graph of the boundary grid of $\pi$ is pure if and only if $\pi$ avoids $2143$. This conjecture concerns a structural characterization of $123$-avoiding permutations through their boundary-grid graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
parsed.source_name: Shyam Narayanan, “Resolving Two Conjectures on Staircase Encodings and Boundary Grids of 132 and 123-avoiding permutations”, arXiv:1802.06345 (2019).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.06345

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2018).

parsed.title: Extremal hyperedge conjecture for FF4-hypergraphs
parsed.statement:
An $FF_{4}$-hypergraph is a $4$-uniform hypergraph in which every set of $5$ vertices contains either $0$ or $2$ hyperedges. Let $\mathcal{H}$ be an $FF_{4}$-hypergraph with $n$ vertices.

**Extremal hyperedge conjecture.** If $n\equiv2\pmod{4}$, then $\mathcal{H}$ has at most

$$
\frac{1}{96}n(n-3)(n+2)(n-2)
$$

hyperedges. If $n\equiv1\pmod{4}$, then $\mathcal{H}$ has at most

$$
\frac{1}{96}(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)(n+3)
$$

hyperedges.

These bounds arise by deleting two vertices from an $FF_{4}$-design of order $n+2$ when $n\equiv2\pmod{4}$, and from one of order $n+3$ when $n\equiv1\pmod{4}$. The source presents the bounds as conjectural extremal values; their general validity is not established there.
parsed.source_name: Wiam Belkouche, Abderrahim Boussaïri, Soufiane Lakhlifi and Mohammed Zaidi, “An exact extremal result for tournaments and 4-uniform hypergraphs”, arXiv:1802.07621 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.07621

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2018).

parsed.title: Sacrifice-size conjecture for cumulative subtraction games
parsed.statement: Let a cumulative subtraction game be played with a finite action set, and suppose optimal play includes sacrifices by both players. **Sacrifice-size conjecture.** In such a game, Negative's sacrifice is smaller than Positive's sacrifice. The claim concerns the relative sizes of sacrifices when both players sacrifice during optimal play; the paper supplies an example with action set $S=\{2,10,13,14\}$ in which Positive sacrifices $4$ and Negative sacrifices $1$. The supplied text gives no evidence of a proof or disproof, so its resolution remains open.
parsed.source_name: Gal Cohensius, Urban Larsson, Reshef Meir and David Wahlstedt, “Cumulative subtraction games”, arXiv:1805.09368 (2020).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.09368

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

parsed.title: Hereditary NP-completeness of cubic-graph coloring targets
parsed.statement:
Let $H$ be a connected cubic graph. The $H$-problem asks, for a connected cubic graph $G$, whether $G$ admits an $H$-coloring. Let $\mathcal{C}_{NP}$ be the class of connected cubic graphs $H$ for which the $H$-problem is NP-complete.

**Hereditary-class conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{C}_{NP}$ is a hereditary class of cubic graphs.

The source motivates this conjecture by comparing the complexity of the $H$-problem for several target graphs, including $S_{10}$, $S_{12}$, $P_{10}$ and $P_{12}$. Its status is left open in the supplied text.
parsed.source_name: Anush Hakobyan and Vahan Mkrtchyan, “S_12 and P_12-colorings of cubic graphs”, arXiv:1807.08138 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.08138

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2018).

parsed.title: Alternating-string conjecture for minimal autocorrelation
parsed.statement:
Let $x$ be a binary string of length $m$, and let $\kappa^2(x)$ denote its autocorrelation coefficient. The alternating string is $x=\texttt{1010...}$.

**Alternating-string conjecture.** The alternating string $x=\texttt{1010...}$ minimizes the autocorrelation coefficient $\kappa^2$.

The paper presents this as an unresolved minimization problem, contrasting it with the proved maximization by the constant all-zero and all-one strings.
parsed.source_name: Arash Atashpendar, David Mestel, A. W. Roscoe and Peter Y. A. Ryan, “A Proof of Entropy Minimization for Outputs in Deletion Channels via Hidden Word Statistics”, arXiv:1807.11609 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.11609

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2018).

parsed.title: Permutation conjecture for a trinomial over fields of characteristic two
parsed.statement:
Let $n=2m$ be a positive integer, and let $f(x)$ be the trinomial defined by equation (1) in the source over ${\mathbb F}_{2^{2m}}$. A pair $(s,t)$ specifies the exponents in this trinomial. **Permutation conjecture.** If

$$
\gcd(m,5)=1\quad\text{and}\quad (s,t)=\left(\frac{4}{11},\frac{10}{11}\right),
$$

then $f(x)$ is a permutation polynomial over ${\mathbb F}_{2^{2m}}$. The paper proves this conjecture by analyzing the quadratic factors of an eleventh-degree polynomial over ${\mathbb F}_{2^n}$, so the claim is solved.
parsed.source_name: Nian Li and Qiaoyu Hu, “A conjecture on permutation trinomials over finite fields of characteristic two”, arXiv:1809.02809 (2018).
parsed.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1708.04841](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.04841), [arXiv:1702.06446](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.06446).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.02809

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2018); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

parsed.title: The Fishburn-Wilf equivalence conjecture for patterns 2413, 2431 and 3241
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathscr{F}_n(\sigma)$ denote the set of Fishburn permutations of length $n$ avoiding the pattern $\sigma$. **Fishburn-Wilf equivalence conjecture.** The three pattern-avoidance classes are equinumerous:

$$
\mathscr{F}_n(2413)\sim \mathscr{F}_n(2431)\sim \mathscr{F}_n(3241).
$$

This conjecture is part of the paper's classification of Wilf equivalence classes for patterns of size four; the source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
parsed.source_name: Juan B. Gil and Michael D. Weiner, “On pattern-avoiding Fishburn permutations”, arXiv:1812.01682 (2019).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.01682

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2018).

parsed.title: The mixed-subdivision strengthening of the planar discrete Brunn–Minkowski conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $A,B\subset\mathbb R^2$ be finite two-dimensional sets. A triangulation $T_A$ of $[A]$ uses $A$ as its vertex set, and a triangulation $T_B$ of $[B]$ uses $B$ as its vertex set. Let $M$ be a corresponding mixed subdivision of $[A+B]$, and let $M_{11}$ denote the set of parallelograms in $M$. **Mixed-subdivision strengthening.** There exist triangulations $T_A$ and $T_B$ and a corresponding mixed subdivision $M$ such that

$$
|M_{11}|\geq \sqrt{|T_A|\cdot |T_B|}.
$$

This is stated as a stronger version of the planar discrete Brunn–Minkowski conjecture. The parser marks it disproved: the paper gives an example showing that one cannot in general fix the triangulations $T_A$ and $T_B$ in the conjecture.
parsed.source_name: Károly J. Böröczky, Máté Matolcsi, Imre Z. Ruzsa, Francisco Santos and Oriol Serra, “Triangulations and a discrete Brunn-Minkowski inequality in the plane”, arXiv:1812.04117 (2018).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.04117

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2018).

parsed.title: Optimal bounds for iterated sumsets with $|5A|=100$
parsed.statement:
Let $A$ be a subset of the integers, with iterated sumsets $hA=\{a_1+\cdots+a_h:a_i\in A\}$, and suppose that $|5A|=100$.

**Optimal sumset bounds conjecture.** Every such set satisfies

$$
|4A|\ge 63\qquad\text{and}\qquad |6A|\le 145.
$$

The example $A=\{0,1,5,8,49\}$ attains both bounds, so the conjecture asserts that the displayed estimates are optimal for finite sets of integers with $|5A|=100$. The source gives strong evidence but no proof or resolution.
parsed.source_name: Shalom Eliahou and Eshita Mazumdar, “Iterated sumsets and Hilbert functions”, arXiv:2006.08998 (2020).
parsed.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1903.03499](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.03499).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08998

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

parsed.title: Kantor's conjecture on strong embeddability of hypermodular matroids
parsed.statement:
We assume all matroids are finite. A matroid is **modular** if every pair of its flats is modular, and **hypermodular** if every pair of its maximal proper flats is modular. A matroid is **strongly embeddable** in a matroid if it is a restriction of that matroid.

**Kantor's conjecture.** Every hypermodular matroid is strongly embeddable in a modular matroid.

This conjecture concerns modular extensions of hypermodular matroids and was made by Kantor in 1974; Bonin later rephrased it. The supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.
parsed.source_name: Jaeho Shin, “The Sticky Matroid Conjecture”, arXiv:2108.04757 (2021).
parsed.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2011.14577](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14577), [arXiv:1704.08478](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.08478).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.04757
